explanation: A binomial experiment is n independent yes/no trials, each a success with probability p; the bars show the chance of getting exactly k successes. The n and p sliders reshape the whole distribution — raising p slides the peak right, and the mean always lands at μ = np (the purple line). The sweeping bar reads out P(X=k) and a conditional probability P(X=k | X≤k), which renormalizes by only the outcomes still possible once you know X≤k — that's exactly what 'given that' does: shrink the sample space, then re-divide.
bullets: P(X=k) = C(n,k)·p^k·(1−p)^(n−k): choose which k trials succeed, times their probability.
The distribution is centered at the mean μ = np.
Conditional P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B): restrict to B, then renormalize.
